en.runTitle: Bristol videographer: a travelling 4K editing laptop for £1,500 or less

en.template: Help me compare {offers} within {budget} for {camera}, {resolve} and {delivery}. Include {extras}, check the delivered basket, and outline a native/proxy test for {timeline}. Ask before buying, contacting sellers or sharing files.

phases.title: Check UK prices, chip and editor support, and independent measurements from public sources
phases.note: Apple, Intel and NVIDIA documentation, Resolve and Premiere codec pages, UK shop prices
phases.judgment: It would not accept a vendor shortcut. Intel’s overview says “10th Gen and newer” can decode 10-bit 4:2:2 video, but Intel’s own detailed table marks only one 10th-generation family, so chips are judged one by one. For the MacBook, Apple’s page does not prove 4:2:2 support, so real playback is flagged as untested.

phases.title: Write the comparison page and the dated source list, with clear recommendations and uncertainties
phases.judgment: It checked the MacBook’s £1,199 price on John Lewis’s own page and set aside tempting search-result prices that were unavailable or much higher there. The three Windows offers and the SSD are labelled provisional, not confirmed bargains. The total is £1,457.99: £1,199 plus a £59 charger and a £199.99 SSD.

phases.title: Test the page at desktop and phone width, then deliver the files

workers: Checked which Apple, Intel and NVIDIA chips decode Sony-style 10-bit 4:2:2 H.265 in hardware, and what Resolve’s free and Studio editions support
Looked for three or four exact UK Windows laptops with NVIDIA graphics under £1,500 and checked public prices, stock and screen limits
